lead: Intuit fell about 10.8% (Reuters, Friday afternoon; close unconfirmed) after agreeing to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68B, under a third of the roughly $12B it paid in 2021, and cutting its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast to 8-9% from 9-10%, on a day the S&P 500 lost 3.59% and the S&P 500 and Dow confirmed corrections.
why: Guidance cut: FY27 revenue forecast lowered to $23.08B-$23.37B (8-9% growth) from $23.28B-$23.51B (9-10%); Credit Karma growth outlook cut to 3-7% from 11-13%; Q2 adjusted EPS guide $3.17-$3.22 vs $3.73 expected. Morgan Stanley called it a 'Credit Karma-led FY27 revenue cut and weak Q2 guide' ($315 -> $310 target); Jefferies, Barclays, UBS and BofA also cut targets.

Mailchimp sale: ~$3.31B cash plus $368M of Bending Spoons stock, closing early 2027; Intuit says it will focus on AI tools for small businesses and use the cash for buybacks. Mailchimp Q1 revenue fell 1% to $313M.

Market backdrop: S&P 500 -3.59% to 6,918.45, Nasdaq -5.13% to 22,654.15, Dow -1.85% (Reuters preliminary close); Anthropic fell about 10% on day two; December hike odds ~95.5% (CME FedWatch). Intuit was already down roughly 54% this year (Yahoo Finance) even as Q1 adjusted EPS rose 56% to $2.91.
